As of September 30, 2025, the Company's leverage ratio was approximately 1.83x, which constituted a technical breach of the covenant. The Company obtained a temporary waiver from the lending syndicate through March 31, 2026, and is in active discussions regarding a permanent amendment to the covenant threshold. ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, EnergyX Corp. reported total revenue of $8.9 billion, a decrease of 12.4% compared to the prior year. The decline was primarily driven by a sustained reduction in realized oil prices, which averaged $68 per barrel during the fiscal year compared to $82 per barrel in the prior year, a decline of approximately 17%. Natural gas revenues were similarly affected, with average realized prices declining 14% year-over-year. Production volumes remained relatively stable at 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, a decrease of 2.1% from the prior year. Operating margin contracted from 22.1% to 14.2%, reflecting the disproportionate impact of commodity price declines on our cost structure, as approximately 65% of our operating costs are fixed or semi-fixed in nature.

The Company continues to face challenges in its upstream reserve base. Proved reserves as of December 31, 2025 stood at 1.2 billion barrels of oil equivalent (BOE), reflecting a reserve replacement ratio of 0.68x for the fiscal year. The below-unity replacement ratio indicates that the Company is depleting its reserve base faster than it is discovering or acquiring new reserves. Management has identified several exploration prospects in the Permian Basin and offshore Gulf of Mexico that are expected to improve the replacement ratio in coming years, contingent upon capital allocation decisions and commodity price recovery.

Note 12 — Debt Covenants and Credit Facilities: The Company maintains a $5.1 billion term loan facility and a $2.0 billion revolving credit facility with a syndicate of 14 lenders. Under the terms of the credit agreement, the Company is required to maintain a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.0x (defined as EBITDA to interest expense). As of December 31, 2025, the Company's interest coverage ratio was approximately 3.2x, providing a cushion of approximately $45 million in EBITDA before a covenant breach would occur. Management notes that the interest coverage ratio has declined from 5.1x at the end of the prior fiscal year due to lower commodity prices and the resulting decline in EBITDA. Should average realized oil prices remain below $70 per barrel through the first quarter of 2026, the Company projects the interest coverage ratio could decline to approximately 2.8x, which would constitute a breach of the covenant. The Company is engaged in preliminary discussions with its lending syndicate regarding a potential amendment to the coverage threshold.

Note 14 — Oil and Gas Reserves (Supplemental): Proved developed reserves decreased 8.2% during the fiscal year to 820 million BOE. Proved undeveloped reserves were 380 million BOE. The reserve replacement ratio of 0.68x reflects 194 million BOE of additions against 285 million BOE of production and revisions. Extensions and discoveries contributed 142 million BOE, while improved recovery added 52 million BOE. Downward revisions of 93 million BOE were recorded, primarily related to economic limit adjustments driven by lower commodity price assumptions.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

BankFirst Financial Group reported net interest income of $1.8 billion for fiscal year 2025, a decrease of 3.8% compared to the prior year. The decline was driven by a 45 basis point compression in net interest margin (NIM) to 2.85%, as the cost of deposits and wholesale funding increased more rapidly than the yield on earning assets. Total deposits declined 2.1% during the year to $22.8 billion, reflecting competitive pressures in the regional banking market and migration of customer balances to higher-yielding money market alternatives. The Company responded by raising deposit rates across its product suite, which contributed to the NIM compression.

Credit quality deteriorated materially during fiscal year 2025. Non-performing loans increased to $692 million, representing 3.8% of total loans outstanding, compared to 1.9% at the end of the prior year. The increase was concentrated in the commercial real estate (CRE) portfolio, particularly office and retail properties experiencing elevated vacancy rates and declining valuations. The provision for credit losses was $285 million for the fiscal year, an increase of 156% from $111 million in the prior year, reflecting management's assessment of continued credit deterioration in the CRE portfolio and broader macroeconomic uncertainty.

Note 7 — Credit Quality and Loan Portfolio: Total loans outstanding were $18.2 billion at December 31, 2025. CRE loans totaled $6.2 billion, representing 34.2% of the total loan portfolio. Of the CRE portfolio, $3.4 billion (55%) is secured by office properties and $1.8 billion (29%) by retail properties. The office loan portfolio has experienced significant stress, with average vacancy rates of 22% among the Company's office property borrowers. Notable exposures include a $180 million construction and permanent loan for Harmon Plaza, a mixed-use development in downtown Portland, Oregon. The anchor tenant at Harmon Plaza, representing 35% of the project's planned rental income, departed in October 2025, and the borrower has been unable to secure a replacement tenant. The loan was placed on non-accrual status in November 2025. Management is evaluating impairment and expects a specific reserve of $40-60 million may be required in Q1 2026. The allowance for credit losses was $485 million at year-end, representing 2.67% of total loans, which management believes is adequate but acknowledges may require additional provisioning.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

PropCore REIT Inc. reported fiscal year 2025 rental income of $1.35 billion, an increase of 2.1% compared to the prior year. The modest growth was achieved despite a challenging operating environment characterized by rising vacancy rates and tenant consolidation across the Company's diversified commercial portfolio. The portfolio comprises approximately 42 million square feet of commercial space across 128 properties in 22 markets. Portfolio occupancy declined to 87.3% at December 31, 2025, from 93.1% at the end of the prior fiscal year, a decrease of 580 basis points. The occupancy decline was driven by several factors, including the departure of WeWork from three properties totaling 420,000 square feet, non-renewals by several mid-size tenants in the Company's suburban office portfolio, and softening demand in the Company's retail strip center assets.

The Company's capital structure includes $4.8 billion in total debt, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.29x. Management acknowledges that leverage is above the Company's long-term target range of 1.5-1.8x and is evaluating strategic alternatives including asset dispositions and a potential equity raise to reduce leverage. The Company's weighted average cost of debt was 5.8% for the fiscal year, an increase of 110 basis points from the prior year, reflecting the impact of higher benchmark rates on the Company's floating-rate borrowings.

Note 15 — Debt and Interest Rate Exposure: Total debt of $4.8 billion includes $2.98 billion (62%) in floating-rate borrowings, primarily consisting of variable-rate term loans and revolving credit facilities indexed to SOFR. The Company estimates that each 25 basis point increase in benchmark interest rates results in approximately $30 million in additional annual interest expense. The Company has entered into interest rate swap agreements covering $800 million of floating-rate exposure through June 2026, but the remaining $2.18 billion of unhedged floating-rate debt represents significant interest rate risk. Management is actively evaluating additional hedging strategies and fixed-rate refinancing opportunities.

Note 18 — Capital Expenditures and Deferred Maintenance: The Company incurred capital expenditures of $85 million during fiscal year 2025, compared to an estimated required run rate of $140 million to maintain the portfolio in its current condition. The cumulative deferred maintenance backlog is estimated at $340 million, primarily related to HVAC systems, roofing, and elevator modernization across the portfolio's older properties. Management has prioritized capital expenditures at properties with near-term lease expirations to maximize tenant retention but acknowledges that the deferred maintenance backlog presents a risk to property valuations and tenant satisfaction.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

ManufactCo Industries Inc. reported fiscal year 2025 revenue of $3.6 billion, an increase of 1.8% compared to the prior year. The modest growth reflects stable demand from the Company's primary defense and aerospace customer base, partially offset by softening in the industrial automation segment. Operating margin was 9.4% for the fiscal year, compared to 10.1% in the prior year. The margin contraction was driven by higher raw material costs, particularly specialty steel and titanium alloys, and labor cost inflation in the Company's manufacturing facilities. The Company employed approximately 14,200 workers across 8 manufacturing facilities in 5 states.

The Company's revenue concentration remains a significant strategic consideration. Approximately 67% of fiscal year 2025 revenue, or $2.41 billion, was derived from contracts and subcontracts with Northrop Grumman Corporation, the Company's largest customer. This concentration reflects ManufactCo's position as a Tier 1 supplier of precision-machined components for multiple Northrop Grumman defense programs. The primary master supply agreement with Northrop Grumman, valued at approximately $2.4 billion over its remaining term, expires in Q2 2026 and is subject to renegotiation. Management is confident in the Company's competitive position for contract renewal but acknowledges that any material change in contract terms could significantly impact future revenue and profitability.

Note 16 — Pension and Other Post-Retirement Benefits: The Company sponsors defined benefit pension plans covering approximately 9,800 current and former employees. As of December 31, 2025, the projected benefit obligation (PBO) was $1.50 billion and the fair value of plan assets was $1.08 billion, resulting in an unfunded status of $420 million (72% funded ratio). The unfunded status increased from $310 million at the end of the prior year, primarily due to a 40 basis point decrease in the discount rate used to measure the obligation (from 5.2% to 4.8%) and lower-than-expected investment returns on plan assets. The Company contributed $45 million to the pension plan during fiscal year 2025 and expects required contributions of $55-65 million in FY2026 under ERISA funding rules. The pension obligation represents the Company's largest single off-balance-sheet liability and is subject to further deterioration if discount rates decline or investment returns underperform actuarial assumptions.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

MedDevice Systems Corp. reported fiscal year 2025 revenue of $2.8 billion, an increase of 6.2% compared to the prior year. Growth was driven by strong performance in the cardiac division, which grew 14% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, and the orthopedic division, which grew 3% to $980 million. The neurostimulation segment contributed $620 million in revenue, up 2% from the prior year. Operating margin was 18.6%, reflecting the Company's premium product mix and manufacturing efficiencies. Net income was $280 million, or $1.60 per diluted share.

The Company's Cardiofix line of cardiac implants experienced a disruption in Q4 2025 following the receipt of an FDA Form 483 observation letter and the initiation of a voluntary field correction. These events are discussed in further detail below and in the accompanying notes.

Note 8 — FDA Regulatory Matters: In November 2025, the FDA issued a Form 483 inspection observation letter to the Company following an inspection of the Cardiofix implant manufacturing facility in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The inspection identified 3 observations related to quality system controls, specifically: (1) inadequate documentation of design change verification for the Cardiofix Model C-400 series, (2) insufficient environmental monitoring in the cleanroom packaging area, and (3) gaps in the corrective and preventive action (CAPA) system for supplier quality deviations. The Company has submitted a corrective action plan to the FDA and is investing approximately $25 million in remediation activities. Additionally, in December 2025, the Company initiated a voluntary field correction affecting approximately 12,000 Cardiofix C-400 units distributed between August and November 2025. The field correction is precautionary and relates to a packaging integrity concern identified during routine quality audits. Revenue of approximately $40 million was deferred from Q4 2025 pending completion of the field correction. The Company does not anticipate a Warning Letter at this time but acknowledges that the FDA's review is ongoing.

Note 11 — Goodwill and Intangible Assets: Goodwill totaled $1.2 billion at December 31, 2025, substantially all of which relates to the acquisition of PulseTech Medical in 2022 for $1.8 billion. PulseTech was acquired for its advanced neurostimulation technology platform and was expected to generate revenue of $950 million by FY2025. Actual PulseTech-related revenue for FY2025 was $620 million, approximately 35% below the acquisition projection. The Company performed its annual goodwill impairment test as of October 1, 2025, and determined that the fair value of the PulseTech reporting unit exceeded its carrying value by only 4%, which is below the Company's threshold for further analysis. Based on updated revenue projections and discount rate assumptions, management expects to record a goodwill impairment charge of approximately $210 million in Q1 2026. This non-cash charge will reduce the carrying value of goodwill but will not affect the Company's cash flows or debt covenants.

Note 19 — Contingencies and Legal Proceedings: The Company is a defendant in approximately 340 pending lawsuits related to its legacy OrthoFlex hip implant system, which was voluntarily recalled in 2020 due to elevated revision rates. Plaintiffs allege design and manufacturing defects resulted in premature implant failure. The Company has accrued $85 million for estimated settlement costs, based on an analysis of resolved claims and pending case characteristics. However, management notes that the ultimate liability could range from $60 million to $180 million depending on trial outcomes and settlement dynamics. The Company's product liability insurance is expected to cover approximately $40 million of the total exposure.
sec_filings.10-Q: For the quarter ended December 31, 2025, MedDevice Systems Corp. reported revenue of $690 million, below the consensus estimate of $710 million. The shortfall was primarily attributable to the voluntary field correction of Cardiofix C-400 units, which resulted in approximately $40 million of deferred revenue. Excluding the field correction impact, revenue would have been approximately $730 million, ahead of estimates. The cardiac division reported Q4 revenue of $270 million, down from $320 million in Q3, reflecting the field correction disruption. Operating margin was 16.8% for the quarter, below the full-year 18.6%, driven by $15 million in remediation costs related to the FDA Form 483 observations and the field correction. Regarding the goodwill impairment assessment, management confirmed that the Q1 2026 impairment charge of approximately $210 million for the PulseTech reporting unit remains the current best estimate, pending final valuation analysis.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

FinTechPay Inc. reported fiscal year 2025 revenue of $1.6 billion, an increase of 24.8% compared to the prior year, reflecting continued momentum in the Company's payments platform. Total payment volume (TPV) processed through the platform reached $142 billion for the fiscal year, an increase of 31% year-over-year. The merchant base grew to approximately 380,000 active merchants, an increase of 22% from the prior year. Net revenue retention was 108%, indicating that existing merchants continue to increase their use of the platform over time. Gross margin was 42.5% for the fiscal year, a decline of 180 basis points from the prior year, reflecting competitive pricing pressure and the impact of merchant incentive programs.

The Company reported a net loss of $85 million for fiscal year 2025, compared to a net loss of $62 million in the prior year. The increased loss was driven by continued investment in technology, sales, and marketing to capture market share in the rapidly evolving payments landscape. Operating margin was -5.3%. Management remains committed to achieving operating profitability by FY2027, contingent upon continued revenue growth and operating leverage in the Company's cost structure. However, the Company acknowledges that the growth deceleration observed in Q3 and Q4 2025 could extend the timeline to profitability if the trend persists.

Note 22 — SEC Inquiry: In October 2025, the Company received an informal inquiry from the staff of the Securities and Exchange Commission regarding the Company's revenue recognition practices. The inquiry is focused on the timing and classification of merchant incentive payments, specifically whether approximately $48 million in merchant sign-up bonuses recorded in Q1 and Q2 2025 should have been recognized ratably over the expected merchant relationship period rather than recognized at the time of contract execution. The Company's current accounting treatment recognizes sign-up bonuses as a reduction to revenue at the time of payment, consistent with its interpretation of ASC 606. The Company is cooperating fully with the SEC staff and has provided requested documentation. Management believes the Company's revenue recognition practices are appropriate and in compliance with GAAP, but acknowledges that the SEC staff may reach a different conclusion. If the SEC were to require restatement, the impact would be a reclassification of approximately $48 million of revenue from Q1/Q2 2025 to later periods, which would reduce the Company's reported first-half growth rate.

Note 25 — Merchant Metrics: Monthly merchant churn increased to 3.8% in Q4 2025 from 2.1% in Q1 2025. The increase in churn was concentrated in the small and micro-merchant segment (annual TPV below $500,000), which represents approximately 45% of the merchant base but only 12% of TPV. Management attributes the churn increase to competitive pricing from new market entrants and the normalization of pandemic-era digital payment adoption. The Company has launched a retention program targeting at-risk merchants and expects churn to stabilize in the 3.0-3.5% range by mid-2026.
sec_filings.10-Q: For the quarter ended December 31, 2025, FinTechPay Inc. reported revenue of $425 million, below the consensus estimate of $445 million by 4.5%. Total payment volume was $38 billion for the quarter, up 22% year-over-year but representing a deceleration from the 35% growth rate in Q1. Monthly merchant churn increased to 3.8%, the highest level since the Company's IPO. Regarding the SEC informal inquiry, the Company continues to cooperate fully with the SEC staff and has not received any indication that the inquiry will be upgraded to a formal investigation. Management reiterated its belief that the Company's accounting practices are appropriate under GAAP.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

LogiFlow Corp. reported fiscal year 2025 revenue of $5.2 billion, an increase of 3.4% compared to the prior year. Growth was driven by modest volume increases across the Company's truckload and less-than-truckload (LTL) segments, partially offset by rate pressure in the spot market. The Company operated a fleet of approximately 18,500 tractors and 52,000 trailers as of December 31, 2025. On-time delivery performance was 94.2% for the fiscal year, consistent with industry standards. Operating margin was 7.8%, compared to 8.3% in the prior year, reflecting higher fuel costs and labor cost inflation.

Fuel costs represented 28.4% of revenue for the fiscal year, compared to 25.1% in the prior year. The Company does not maintain a formal fuel hedging program and is therefore exposed to fluctuations in diesel prices. Management estimates that every $10 per barrel change in crude oil prices impacts annual fuel costs by approximately $65 million. The Company recovers a portion of fuel cost increases through fuel surcharge programs, but the recovery typically lags actual cost increases by 30-60 days.

Note 13 — Contract Concentration: The Company's three largest customers accounted for approximately 38% of fiscal year 2025 revenue, or $1.98 billion. The Company's largest customer relationship is with Amazon.com, Inc., which contributed approximately $1.1 billion in revenue under a master transportation services agreement that expires in June 2026. The second-largest customer is Walmart Inc., contributing approximately $520 million under an agreement expiring in September 2026. The third-largest is Target Corporation, contributing approximately $360 million under an agreement expiring in November 2026. The simultaneous renewal of all three major contracts within a single calendar year represents a concentrated risk. Management is in preliminary discussions with all three customers regarding renewal terms and is confident in the Company's competitive position, but acknowledges that pricing pressure and volume commitments are subject to negotiation.

Note 17 — Labor Relations and Collective Bargaining: Approximately 8,400 of the Company's drivers are represented by Teamsters Local 952 under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA) that expires on March 31, 2026. The prior CBA negotiation in 2022 resulted in a 14-day work stoppage before a new agreement was ratified, with an estimated revenue impact of $45 million and additional costs of $12 million for service recovery and customer retention incentives. Management has commenced preliminary discussions with union leadership regarding the upcoming renewal and has budgeted for wage increases of 4-6% and enhanced benefit provisions. However, the union has publicly stated its intent to seek wage increases of 8-10% and improvements to scheduling and safety provisions, creating a significant gap between the parties' positions.
sec_filings.10-Q: For the quarter ended December 31, 2025, LogiFlow Corp. reported revenue of $1.29 billion, slightly ahead of the consensus estimate of $1.28 billion. The modest beat was driven by a late-quarter surge in holiday shipping volumes. Operating margin was 7.5% for the quarter, below the full-year average of 7.8%, as diesel prices averaged $4.15 per gallon during the quarter compared to $3.85 in the prior quarter. Regarding the Amazon contract renewal, management noted that discussions have progressed to the term sheet stage and that the Company is optimistic about continuation of the relationship, though at potentially lower per-unit rates reflecting increased automation at Amazon fulfillment centers. The Teamsters CBA negotiation is scheduled to begin formally in January 2026, with the current agreement expiring March 31, 2026.

The outcome will significantly shape LogiFlow's financial trajectory.

news.summary: Teamsters Local 952 is preparing for contract negotiations with LogiFlow Corp., with the current collective bargaining agreement expiring March 31, 2026. The 2022 negotiation resulted in a 14-day work stoppage that cost LogiFlow an estimated $45 million in lost revenue.

Analysts estimate that every $10 per barrel change in oil prices impacts LogiFlow's annual costs by approximately $65 million, with only partial recovery through fuel surcharges.

Several competitors have announced partnerships with autonomous vehicle companies, with limited commercial deployments beginning on high-volume interstate routes. Analysts noted that LogiFlow's heavy reliance on unionized drivers could become a cost disadvantage as autonomous technology matures.
